findings.finding: The classifier compares the current proof-stage log SHA with the whole-log SHA stored on the prior S3 target row. `match_first_and_only_error` requires `target.log_sha256 == sha(log_text)`, but `_classify` computes `log_observation.log_sha256` from the newly executed matrix log while target_map rows carry the S3 log digest. Those logs contain elapsed timestamps, so a fresh run with the same exact diagnostic normally has a different whole-file digest and is classified CONTROL_FAILURE_TARGET_MISMATCH; the seven negative rows cannot complete the matrix.
findings.fix: Keep the prior observation artifact SHA/provenance attached to the prior target-map record. Match the current stage log against the exact diagnostic fields without requiring its whole-file digest to equal the prior artifact digest. Record/hash the current log separately and bind it to the current stage output. If a content-derived stable digest is needed for the diagnostic, hash the exact normalized diagnostic line separately from the full artifact.

findings.finding: `_classify` constructs the current `log_observation` by copying `target_map[variant].provenance` (the prior S3 build/archive/request provenance) into the current-log observation. The current stage identity is separately checked for argv/source/gates/log filename, but no current-stage build/artifact provenance is associated with that current log hash. This mixes prior target provenance into a current observation and does not establish the current log provenance. The audit also checks current observation SHA against row SHA but does not distinguish or validate a current-stage provenance record against the prior pin.
findings.fix: Keep two explicit records: prior target observation provenance from S3, and current stage/log identity from the current stage receipt. Do not copy the former into the latter. Have the audit require both and preserve their distinct roles; current log path/hash must be bound to the current stage record while the target map remains a prior observed expectation.

nits: The packet reports the current positive row still fails on dead-code diagnostics. Even after the target-log issue is fixed, this candidate cannot yield a complete matrix until a clean positive run is separately established.
